messages:
tim_customer: Hey team — noticing a pretty big mismatch between the usage dashboard and our invoice for the Mar billing window. Dashboard shows ~60k tokens served, invoice shows ~120k billed. Account: acme-prod. Any idea what could cause this?

sarah_support: Sorry about that — can you share the invoice id and a few example request IDs or timestamps so we can trace?

tim_customer: Invoice ID inv_2026_03_acme_42. Sample request IDs (from our app logs): req_ab12, req_cd34, req_ef56. Time window: 2026-03-12 14:00-15:30 UTC. I also see a spike in Billed Tokens in the invoice CSV around 14:02.

alex_eng: jumping in. Quick Q: which model + routing config were you using? Any prefetch / warmup flags enabled (kvcache.prefetch, continuous-batcher)?

tim_customer: model: gptx-8k, routing: continuous-batcher enabled on dedicated pool, kvcache.prefetch: true (default). No special manual warmup.

alex_eng: thanks — I'm seeing some traces for that timeframe. There are a bunch of background prefetch calls tagged by the runtime as `prefetch` that look like they were issued by the continuous coalescing batcher warmup routine. Important: the metering pipeline currently charges tokens at ingest time. Those prefetch calls are ingested as independent requests and get billed, but our served-token dashboard (which aggregates per-response attribution) collapses them differently, so they don't show up in the per-request served numbers.

alex_eng: short log snippet from infra traces:
```
2026-03-12T14:02:03.123Z prefetch_request id=req_ab12 api_key=acct_acme tokens=423 tag=prefetch source=cbatcher
2026-03-12T14:02:04.200Z coalesced_batch id=batch_987 included=[req_ab12, req_cd34] total_tokens=512
2026-03-12T14:02:04.205Z response_served id=req_ab12 served_by=batch_987 tokens=89
```

alex_eng: The prefetch produced ~423 tokens of warmup text (billed at ingest). Later the coalesced batch served shorter output for the real client request (89 tokens). Invoice shows the 423 + 89, dashboard only surfaces the 89 in served metrics because it attributes the final served response to the request. That discrepancy matches the ~2x factor you reported.

sarah_support: Understood. Is this a bug or expected behavior with continuous-batcher + kvcache.prefetch?

alex_eng: It's currently expected behavior given how prefetch is implemented (background, separate logical request), but it's not the UX we want — we should not surprise customers with hidden warmup billing. Two parts: 1) short-term mitigation (config change), 2) longer-term fix (metering dedupe / attribution changes).

alex_eng: Short repro steps to reproduce locally:
1) Start dedicated runtime with continuous-batcher enabled and kvcache.prefetch=true.
2) Send a small number of client requests with long prefix context to trigger KV warmup.
3) Observe metering stream: prefetch requests show large token counts at ingest, while final served responses are smaller.

Commands (dev box):
```bash
# start runtime with prefetch enabled
REDWOOD_RUNTIME_OPTS='--continuous-batcher --kvcache.prefetch=true' ./run_local_runtime.sh
# fire 3 requests that cause prefetch warmup
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"input":"<long historical context>"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate
# tail metering events
jq -c '.event_type=="meter"' /var/log/redwood/metering.log | grep prefetch
```

alex_eng: temporary mitigation: set `kvcache.prefetch=false` or reduce `prefetch_rate` to 0 for your key/pool to prevent background warmup calls. We'll also add an internal ticket to dedupe prefetch tokens in billing.

mike_billing: Confirming — our billing pipeline currently sums token counts from ingest records (stream). We do not yet perform semantic deduplication between a prefetch ingest and a later served response for the same logical client action. Because prefetch uses the same api_key, it ends up in the invoice. We can issue an interim invoice credit while eng implements a permanent fix. Please confirm invoice id and timeframe to credit.

tim_customer: Thanks — please credit inv_2026_03_acme_42 for the window 2026-03-12 14:00-15:30 UTC. The amount is roughly the delta between billed and dashboard values (~60k tokens).

mike_billing: Got it. I'll open a billing reconciliation: ticket BILL-2026-789. We will: 1) mark inv_2026_03_acme_42 for review, 2) apply a one-time credit for the documented delta, 3) follow up with a short writeup for the invoice note.

alex_eng: internal action items for engineering:
- ENG-INC-2026-345: add dedupe rule in metering aggregator for `prefetch` tags when a matching served response is later observed within a short window.
- ENG-PR-7421: make kvcache.prefetch default off for newly provisioned dedicated pools and add clear docs/console flag.

sarah_support: I created INC-2026-345 and linked the billing ticket. I'll keep you posted, tim. For now if you want immediate relief, toggle kvcache.prefetch=false on the pool.

tim_customer: toggled prefetch off — will monitor. Thanks for the quick triage.

deploy-bot: Incident created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-INC-2026-345 (assigned to alex_eng).
